Fix conflates 'default_ordering flag' with 'ordering derived from Meta.ordering'; since default_ordering stays True even when the user calls explicit .order_by(), the new guard also suppresses adding explicit order-by columns to GROUP BY, changing aggregation results for that common case instead of narrowly targeting Meta.ordering fallback.

The patch fixes the reported skipped-test symptom but does so by discarding the `_explicit_tearDown` deferral mechanism and inspecting unittest's private `_outcome.skipped`, which changes when tearDown runs under --pdb and over-suppresses runtime skips. The established idiomatic fix is to guard the existing swap with `not _is_skipped(self.obj)` (checking `__unittest_skip__`); this rewrite is fragile and regression-prone.

The functional optimization is correct — the first added AlterModelManagers branch correctly reduces CreateModel + AlterModelManagers to a single CreateModel. However, the same identical elif block is inserted FIVE times, and four of those copies are unreachable dead code, which a Django maintainer would refuse to merge.

The patch overloads the core `contains_aggregate` property to also report window/over clauses, which is the wrong abstraction (window functions are not aggregates and this property drives GROUP BY/HAVING decisions ORM-wide), and it introduces an operator-precedence bug that crashes on None source expressions. The real fix belongs in the aggregation/subquery-wrapping logic, not here.

Fix correctly resolves the PermutationGroup case by mapping inverted generator symbols back through domain.generators, but it also deletes the `elif s**-1 in images` fallback unconditionally, removing handling for inverted generator letters in the non-PermutationGroup (FpGroup) branch where s=r[i] is used directly.

Patch correctly clears the PK for the single-instance fast-delete early-return path, matching Django's intended fix for the reported no-dependency case. However it is incomplete: the regular (non-fast) deletion path still leaves stale PKs, so the general principle 'PK should be None after .delete()' is only half-applied, creating inconsistent behavior between fast and regular deletes.

Adds get/set_antialiased storage and accessors to Text, but the diff never wires self._antialiased into the drawing path (e.g. via the GraphicsContext), so the setter has no effect on actual rendering and the issue's core requirement is unmet.

Core fix is correct: get_feature_names (and inverse_transform) now call _validate_vocabulary() before _check_vocabulary(), resolving the NotFittedError-when-vocabulary-provided issue consistently. However the patch also inserts a redundant duplicate of the existing 'if not hasattr(self, vocabulary_): self._validate_vocabulary()' block in transform, which is dead no-op code that a maintainer would reject.

The one-character `>`→`>=` change correctly fixes the mincnt>=1 inconsistency, but because the preceding `if mincnt is None: mincnt = 0` is left unchanged, the default case (mincnt unspecified, C provided) now evaluates `len(acc) >= 0`, which is always true and invokes reduce_C_function on empty bins. This regresses the documented 'at least one datum' default and breaks/changes behavior for empty cells.

Fix uses functools.wraps correctly so inspect.signature works, but the patch leaves the original manager_method definition in place and adds a second decorated one, producing a duplicated dead function. Functionally correct yet sloppy enough that a maintainer would push back.

However the methods are inserted before each class docstring (demoting it to dead code) and the Remove-then-Add collapse can silently drop a differently-defined index sharing the same name.

Functionally correct for the report, but a Django maintainer would reject this approach in favor of the trivial idiomatic fix.

Code change is correct, minimal, and resolves the issue by threading fill_value through to the initial SimpleImputer. However it adds a public parameter with no docstring entry or versionadded directive, which scikit-learn requires (and numpydoc validation enforces) before merge.

The patch silences the warning by calling self._check_feature_names(X, reset=True) on the internally-validated ndarray, which has the side effect of deleting the fitted feature_names_in_ attribute. This trades the spurious warning for a real regression in fitted-estimator state.

The patch stops the crash for the trivial ascending-F case but is the wrong fix: it coerces an OrderBy into `field.expression.name`, discarding the OrderBy's direction and expression semantics, and breaks on expressions without a `.name`. The proper fix preserves the OrderBy object in `find_ordering_name` rather than flattening it to a string in `get_order_dir`.

The dedup-by-name-on-first-yield approach stops duplicate reporting but yields the intermediate, pre-substitution hashed_name for adjustable files (exactly the base.css case in the bug report), since every adjustable path is already marked processed during the initial single pass and the multi-pass loop's later, corrected hashed_name is then silently dropped. This produces incorrect '<file> as <hash>' output and would feed subclasses (WhiteNoise, S3 backends) the wrong intermediate file instead of the final one, which is the exact regression the original issue warned about.

Fix correctly avoids axes.set_prop_cycle so CN color references work and the global cycler is no longer mutated, resolving the core issue. However it replaces the cycler-based iteration with a plain iter(colors), silently dropping the documented behavior that a shorter colors list repeats/cycles through the stacked layers.

Fix replaces unescape+length-math with a char-by-char strip loop that never strips ';', which does resolve the entity-splitting bug but as a side effect disables trimming of literal (non-entity) trailing semicolons that TRAILING_PUNCTUATION_CHARS was also meant to catch, e.g. 'example.com;' no longer trims the semicolon into trail.

The patch wires up the previously-ignored tzinfo, but resolves the zone name via self.tzinfo.tzname(None), which is a fragile approach that diverges from the project's existing get_tzname() helper. For common tzinfo types this yields an abbreviation/LMT/None rather than the IANA zone name, producing wrong or no-op results outside the narrow case exercised by the test.

The patch correctly generalizes the valid-element count to multiple dims (np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()), but it folds the array-masking branch under `if hasattr(axis, "__len__")`, so single-dimension reductions (integer axis) no longer hit it and fall through to the scalar `elif` branch — silently breaking per-element min_count masking for the common single-dim case. The correct fix keeps the `if axis is not None and getattr(result, "ndim", False)` gate and only swaps `mask.shape[axis]` for `np.take(mask.shape, axis).prod()`.

Patch fixes the migrate symptom by flushing after every OutputWrapper.write(), but takes the wrong approach: the actual bug is that OutputWrapper.flush() is a TextIOBase no-op (never delegates to self._out), and forcing a flush on every write introduces a real performance regression for high-volume commands. Django's accepted fix overrides flush() instead.

The unsigned→signed data conversion for `_Unsigned=False` is correct and the values now decode properly, but the `warnings.warn` call ends up inside the new `elif` branch (16-space indent, no `else`), so it fires the misleading 'not of integer type, ignoring attribute' warning right after a successful conversion and is no longer emitted for genuinely non-integer `_Unsigned` variables.

The middle hunk correctly fixes the issue by adding Combinable.MOD to the different-type numeric operand block, which is the actual fix needed. However, the first and third hunks each add a duplicate Combinable.MOD to tuples that already contain it — functionally harmless (dict-comprehension keys dedupe) but clearly erroneous and would not be merged as-is.

The patch fixes the reported symmetric sum-of-even-powers case, but instead of forwarding `permute` to the recursive `diophantine(eq, param)` call it reimplements permutation handling by blindly applying `signed_permutations` to every solution. That diverges from diophantine's type-specific permute logic and will yield incorrect/spurious solutions for non-symmetric equation types (e.g. binary_quadratic) when syms order differs.

The patch correctly adds self.save_m2m() to persist ManyToMany data, but does so in a second redundant `if commit:` block that calls user.save() a second time, so the user is saved twice. The fix should have added save_m2m() to the existing if-block instead.

Patch resolves the boolean-X TypeError by casting X to float, but places the cast inside `_huber_loss_and_gradient`, which the L-BFGS optimizer calls repeatedly, so X is re-copied to float64 on every iteration. Correct fix belongs in `fit` via `check_X_y(..., dtype=[np.float64, np.float32])`, matching `LinearRegression`.

The one-line change from `>` to `>=` fixes the reported mincnt inconsistency for mincnt>=1, but because `mincnt` still defaults to 0 when unspecified, the comparison `len(acc) >= 0` is now always true, so `reduce_C_function` gets invoked on genuinely empty bins instead of being skipped. This crashes for common reduce functions like `np.min`/`np.max` (ValueError on empty array) and produces spurious RuntimeWarnings even for the default `np.mean`, whereas previously empty bins were guaranteed to bypass the reduction entirely.

The patch makes SQLite's alter_field a noop whenever choices differ, but it short-circuits with OR, so an AlterField that changes choices AND a real schema attribute (max_length, null, etc.) in the same operation is silently skipped, leaving the column unaltered. Wrong layer and approach — the correct fix strips non-db attrs (choices, help_text, verbose_name, validators…) inside _field_should_be_altered, not a SQLite-only choices hack.

The patch relaxes the constraint-count guard from `!= 1` to `< 1`, which suppresses the crash but then unconditionally deletes only `constraint_names[0]` when multiple constraints match — and the introspection order is non-deterministic, so it may drop the unique_together's backing index instead of the intended index_together index. The correct, idiomatic fix is to make the lookup precise (pass `unique=False` in the `index` deletion path so exactly one constraint is found), keeping the strict guard intact.

Fix correctly resolves the reported multi-line case by skipping the first line's zero indent, but omits the `default=0` guard, so `min()` now runs over an empty sequence for single-line docstrings and raises `ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence`. This is a real regression on a very common docstring form.

Patch special-cases `lookups[0] == 'in'` to collapse a MultiColSource into a single column, which resolves the reported subquery-column-count error but breaks legitimate multi-column relations. For composite/ForeignObject `__in` lookups that genuinely need all target columns, selecting only `targets[0]` yields incorrect filtering.

Fix makes comma-splitting bracket-aware so regexes with commas inside `(){}[]` (e.g. `(foo{1,3})`) survive parsing, resolving the reported crash. But it hand-rolls a fragile bracket counter and drops the whitespace-stripping that `_csv_transformer` previously applied, changing behavior for existing `a, b` style configs.

The patch changes lookup_allowed()'s final relational check to match ANY prefix of relation_parts instead of the full relation path, which both fails to address the root cause (relation_parts still drops the 'place' hop for FK-as-PK during list-building) and dangerously loosens the DisallowedModelAdminLookup security guard. It edits the wrong location and introduces a permissive regression.

The patch emits `source-read` during `resolve_references` (post-parse/write phase) with `doctree.astext()` and discards the return value, so it does not modify any source or feed anything back into the doctree — the include'd content is never actually replaced. It also violates the event contract (handlers expect a mutable list `[text]`, not a bare string), which would crash real `source-read` handlers like the one in the bug report.

Small patch adds classmethod-property handling in MethodDocumenter and PropertyDocumenter, and tests pass. However the PropertyDocumenter.can_document_member addition is logically redundant (its second disjunct is a subset of the existing inspect.isproperty check), signaling a confused/incomplete fix mechanism, plus formatting nits.

The patch replaces factorize's unique levels with `lev.astype(var.dtype)` (the full, non-deduplicated level index) rather than casting the factorized uniques. This works for the reported unique-coordinate case but silently corrupts values or raises for non-unique level coordinates, since `split_labels` (codes) index into deduplicated uniques while `levels` is now the full array.

The BoundField-based refactor of value access via `bf.value()` is correct, but collapsing the FileField isinstance branch into a single `bf.field.clean(value, bf.initial)` call passes a second positional arg to every field's clean(), which base `Field.clean(self, value)` does not accept (only FileField.clean takes initial). This raises TypeError for all non-FileField fields during validation.

Fix correctly resolves the stale-LEVEL_TAGS bug by resolving tags lazily per access instead of at import time, so @override_settings is honored. Main concern is removal of the module-level LEVEL_TAGS symbol (backward-compat) plus a stray blank line.

Change tries to preserve input dtypes on pandas output but is fundamentally broken: it references an undefined `dtypes` variable in the default branch (NameError) and unconditionally forces output back to input dtypes, corrupting transformers that modify values. Not mergeable.

The one-liner makes 'documented' call modify_field_list, which fixes the visible missing-return-type symptom but also makes 'documented' add :type:/:param: entries for UNDOCUMENTED parameters — collapsing the semantic distinction between 'documented' and 'all'. A maintainer aware of the config semantics would not merge as-is.

Fix resolves the MultiOutputClassifier AttributeError, but discriminates meta-estimators via hasattr(estimator, 'estimators_'), which is too broad and mis-handles ensembles whose estimators_ are not per-label.

Patch sets formfield.initial for UUIDField in formfield_for_dbfield, but this does not address the reported bug (the to_field target `id` is editable=False, so it never gets a formfield in the inline/admin form) and introduces a regression by assigning the NOT_PROVIDED sentinel as initial when a UUIDField has no default. Wrong layer and incorrect approach.

Patch fixes the reported symptom by nulling `.axes` on children during cla(), but the linked issue explicitly asks to unset BOTH `.axes` and `.figure`, and only `.axes` is handled. Core reported behavior is resolved; the `.figure` half of the request is left incomplete.

Patch inverts the result for the negated case: it sets sql='1=1' on EmptyResultSet but then falls through to the `if self.negated: sql='NOT {}'` wrapper, yielding 'NOT 1=1' (always FALSE) for `~Exists(none())` — the exact reported case, which should evaluate TRUE. This is a correctness bug that leaves the issue effectively unfixed (query still returns empty instead of the name='test' rows).

Patch stops the IndexError but only by bounds-guarding the `del`, which masks the real defect: `blocks`/`num_blocks` shrink during iteration while `rep_blocks` does not, so index `i` desyncs across the three parallel lists. When the guard skips a delete, the non-minimal block system stays in `blocks`, so `minimal_blocks()` can silently return a non-minimal result instead of crashing.

The one-liner adds `& finite` to the `even` rule so `even -> finite` now holds, fixing the reported case. But it only patches `even`; `odd` (defined symmetrically as `integer & !even`) is left unchanged, so `Symbol(odd=True).is_finite` is still None and the asymmetry lets an infinite integer be wrongly inferred as odd.

Fix flips the public default `check_rank=False` → `True` so `hermite_normal_form` no longer silently drops rows on rank-deficient input; a defensible correctness-over-speed default change, but the docstring still documents the old default and the change was not otherwise noted. Second diff hunk is a whitespace-only no-op.

Patch tries to make backward rename restore the old auto-generated name, but for an unnamed (old_fields) index self.old_name is None and the auto-generated name is never stored in state, so `get_index_by_name(self.old_name)` cannot recover it. Django's actual fix kept backward as a no-op for old_fields and instead made forward re-detect the current index by column via `_constraint_names`, making re-apply idempotent-safe; this approach is the wrong abstraction.

The patch only guards `_aggregate_score_dicts` against an empty score list, masking the IndexError symptom rather than fixing the root cause: the generator passed as `cv` is exhausted after the first `cross_val_score` call inside SequentialFeatureSelector's candidate loop. It prevents the crash but leaves SFS scoring most feature candidates against an empty CV, silently producing nan/arbitrary selections.

The center-handling logic is incorrect and fragile: because `starts[:window]=0` is applied before subtracting `offset`, the first windows get negative start indices that rely on Python's negative-index slice emptiness, and the label-reassignment produces duplicated left labels while silently dropping the right-edge windows, so manual iteration still does not reproduce `rolling(center=True).mean()`.

The patch adds a MatrixSymbol-only special case to _print_Add, but a bare MatrixSymbol always has coefficient +1, so the new branch never emits a '-' and produces identical output to the old code; the actual negative terms in the issue (`-A*B`, `-B`) are MatMul objects, not MatrixSymbol, so they are not handled at all. The approach cannot resolve the reported bug and is likely non-functional (also risks a NameError if MatrixSymbol is not imported in str.py).

The patch tries to undo newline translation after the fact via blind string replacement instead of preventing the translation at the source (open the capture buffer with newline=""). This unconditionally rewrites every '\n' to '\r\n', corrupting genuine newlines in all captured output — a broad regression and a fragile, incorrect approach.

Patch special-cases IndexVariables in Dataset.copy to skip the copy that casts '<U*' to object, but it only touches dataset.py while the issue also reports DataArray.copy (ds.z.copy) casting unicode indices — that path lives in dataarray.py and copies coords via v.copy(deep=deep) directly, so it remains broken. Sharing the original IndexVariable object also skips genuine copying (attrs/encoding aliasing) rather than fixing the root cause in IndexVariable.copy.

The patch does not fix the reported bug and is logically inverted: it adds a condition to OMIT storage when the callable returns default_storage, whereas the issue requires the callable reference to always be INCLUDED. It also re-invokes the callable during deconstruct, introducing non-determinism and side effects.

Patch adds a hardcoded non-standard `Proxy-Connection: keep-alive` header inside `HTTPProxyAuth.__call__`, but the reported bug uses `proxies=` dict where proxy auth flows through `rebuild_proxies`/`proxy_headers`, not `HTTPProxyAuth`, so this code path is not even exercised by the repro. Wrong location, non-standard header, and unconditional injection make it a fragile, likely non-fixing change.

The added `if M.shape[i] > 0:` guards are functionally a no-op: `for i in range(0)` already iterates zero times, so wrapping the loops changes nothing and does not alter the computed shape. The change neither fixes the reported dense Matrix.hstack/vstack shape bug (which lives in the matrix join code, not BlockMatrix.shape) nor prevents any IndexError, since the guards sit on the wrong dimension relative to the indexing `M[i,0]`/`M[0,i]`.

Patch resolves the reported `__in` + alias/annotate case by clearing the select clause, but it does so unconditionally for every query compiled through `Query.as_sql` (i.e. all subqueries), not just the `__in` RHS. Clearing column selection this broadly—and as a mutating side effect inside `as_sql`—is an unsafe generalization that a Django maintainer would want scoped to the lookup path.

The warning text says structured arrays will become Columns 'in future versions,' but the code already changes the behavior to Column(data) immediately — a self-contradicting, premature breaking change that ignores the issue's explicit two-stage plan (warn now, change in 5.2).

The patch is logically a no-op: `hasattr(expression, 'filterable') and not expression.filterable` is semantically identical to the original `not getattr(expression, 'filterable', True)` for the reported case (a model instance whose `filterable` field is False), so it still raises NotSupportedError and does not fix the bug. The correct fix must restrict the check to actual expressions (e.g. gate on `hasattr(expression, 'resolve_expression')`), not on the presence of a `filterable` attribute.

The diff swaps `nargs="*"` for `nargs=argparse.REMAINDER` in dbshell.py, but the reported bug (extra parameters placed AFTER the dbname in the psql command) is caused by argument ordering in the PostgreSQL backend client (settings_to_cmd_args_env), not by how dbshell collects parameters. This change does not move parameters before the database name and therefore does not resolve the issue.

Patch adds ensure_ascii=False to json.dumps(not self.is_required) in AutocompleteMixin, but that argument is a boolean whose serialization never contains non-ASCII characters, so the change has zero effect on the reported JSONField unicode display bug. Wrong location entirely — real fix belongs in JSONField.prepare_value (django/forms/fields.py), not the admin autocomplete widget.

The patch fixes the crash by quoting table names, correctly resolving the reserved-word failure, but it hardcodes MySQL-style backticks instead of using Django's standard SQLite identifier quoting (quote_name / double quotes). It works functionally since SQLite accepts backticks, but is inconsistent with repo convention.

The patch modifies `post_mortem` in debugging.py to use `sys.exit` instead of `outcomes.exit`, which is entirely unrelated to the linked issue (interpreter crash on debug builds from `Expression.compile("False")` in the mark expression evaluator). It fixes nothing in the reported bug and replaces pytest's controlled exit mechanism with a raw SystemExit.

Adds violation_error_code plumbing to BaseConstraint and forwards it to the ValidationError raise sites, which resolves the core request. But it omits updating deconstruct() and __eq__, so the new attribute is lost in migration serialization and two constraints differing only by code compare equal.

The quantile fix itself is correct and resolves the issue, but the diff also silently modifies sortby, which has no `keep_attrs` parameter in its signature — referencing `keep_attrs` there raises NameError on every sortby call. That is an unrelated, broken change that would break existing behavior.

The patch adds a defensive `iscoroutine` check in `get_response_async`, but this runs AFTER the outermost (first) middleware has already executed its `process_response`, so it does not stop that middleware from receiving a coroutine — the actual reported symptom. It fixes the wrong layer (boundary return value) instead of the root cause in `MiddlewareMixin`, which must await its async inner `get_response` before invoking `process_response`.
